handoff: Changes requested, 1 blocking bug: a workflow file with a dotted step name makes loadWorkflowText throw a TypeError at derived-counters.ts:40 (edge.split('.')) instead of reporting the file as corrupt. AC1–AC12 traced; unit tier and typecheck green; AC12 runs in CI.

findings.title: A dotted step name in a workflow file crashes the loader instead of being reported as corrupt
findings.detail:
deriveEdgeCounters runs on the parsed YAML before any schema check and keys each edge as `${step}.${outcome}`. withDerivedCounters then recovers the step with `edge.split(".")` (line 40) and reads `(steps[step] as Obj).outcomes` (line 41). For a step named `a.b` with `fail: implement`, the key `a.b.fail` splits to step `a`. `steps.a` is undefined, so the loader throws `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'steps[step].outcomes')`. Repro: call loadWorkflowText("w", text, "/repo/.agents/workflows/w.yaml", "checkout", "/repo") on `name: w / start: implement / steps: { implement: { agent: Build it., outcomes: { done: a.b }, means: { done: x } }, a.b: { check: bun test, timeout: 5m, outcomes: { pass: $done, fail: implement } } }`. It throws instead of returning { ok: false, reason: "corrupt" }. loadFile → loadWorkflows (config.ts:406–411) catches nothing, despite its doc 'invalid files are reported, not thrown'. AGENTS.md › Rules: 'a failing file makes the unit corrupt, never a guess'. Before this change the same file was refused at /steps by the step-name pattern. A dotted outcome name does not crash, but it is mis-split the same way.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Carry step and outcome separately in DerivedCounting.edges (for example a list of { step, outcome, counter }) instead of re-splitting the joined name. Or skip deriving when a step or outcome name does not match its pattern, and leave the refusal to the schema check that follows. Add a test that a dotted step name is refused as corrupt, not thrown.
